abstract: Primary root morphogenesis is coordinated by the integrated action of cell division, expansion, and differentiation. Although auxin is a central regulator of root development, how the spatial context of auxin perception shapes growth dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we implement a synthetic auxin perception system that enables tissue-specific manipulation of auxin signaling output in defined spatial domains of the Arabidopsis thaliana root. Using this approach, we show that root growth depends primarily on the integration of local auxin perception in elongating cells of the outermost root tissue layers. Computational modeling predicts that mutually exclusive auxin sensitivity domains shift the position of the cell proliferation boundary, which was validated experimentally. We further found that elongating cells exhibit greater sensitivity to auxin input than meristematic cells, and that this differential responsiveness is critical for determining the overall root length. Together, our results identify mutually exclusive spatial domains of auxin sensitivity that coordinate root morphogenesis.
